column1: # Proof that each SCHEDULED workflow was observed GREEN before it merged.
# A scheduled workflow is the one kind of CI that merges WITHOUT executing: the PR
# goes green on the checks it did not change, the workflow first runs hours later on
# a cron, and the result lands in a tab nobody opens. nightly-netem merged that way
# and was red on its very first cron run, then 19 of its first 21.
# So: change a workflow with an `on: schedule:` trigger and you must dispatch it on
# your branch, watch it go GREEN, and record that run here.
# scripts/check_scheduled_workflow_proof.py resolves the run id through the GitHub
# API and checks it is a green `workflow_dispatch` run OF THIS WORKFLOW — the row is
# a claim, and the gate verifies the claim rather than trusting it.
# The head sha TRAILS the PR head by design: the dispatch necessarily runs before the
# commit that records its id. It names which tree was proven.

column5: the COMPOSED arm added: all four conditions at once, which no arm had ever driven together. Dispatched green before merge — 5 netem arms + flakynet, all success. The composed arm closes a coverage gap and buys NO early warning of the field wedge (loopback's capacity is never the constraint); a netem-rate arm was tried and left out because its red named the placement leg, not a consensus deadline.
